answer: An agent marketplace can require every seller to lock a $100 bond for 30 days, forfeited if a public audit proves it sold the same exclusive asset twice. Transaction records act as a lantern for auditors, so fresh names offer no haven from evidence tied to each sale. Attackers can let a thousand bots wander the market, but activating them ties up $100,000; abandoning a caught identity sacrifices its bond, and replacing it requires fresh capital.
